title: rotary-embedding-phase-misalignment-under-speculative-batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After enabling speculative batching and the new kernel remapping path for tiled attention, we observed token-level permutation and small-but-accumulating floating-point divergence in outputs vs baseline for long-context decoder runs. Root cause appears to be phase misalignment of rotary/positional computation when a speculative batch merges requests with different prefix lengths and the remapped kernel reorders attention tiles for throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Start local runtime with kernel remapping enabled (ENV KERNEL_REMAP=1) and speculative batching window=5ms,
3) Run reproduce script reproducer/rotary_phase_test.py against decode endpoint using a 16k-context Llama-like model (config: rotary_base=10000, chunk_tile=64),
4) Compare token sequences and logits against control run with KERNEL_REMAP=0 and batching disabled (speculative=0).
observed_behavior: Token-level reordering in ~0.8% of test traces for long-context generation; logits diverge by 1e-3 to 1e-2 per-token over extended generations leading to downstream hallucinations in a few samples. Reproduction is flaky under low QPS but becomes consistent under sustained load with small speculative windows.
expected_behavior: No token permutation and outputs should be bitwise-near or numerically within acceptable tolerance of baseline for deterministic kernels; speculative batching should not change rotary embedding phase for merged requests.
impact: High — affects hosted and dedicated customers using speculative batching or kernel remap. Could cause subtle output drift and rare incorrect generations for long-decoding sequences. Potential customer escalations for reliability-sensitive apps.
diagnosis: Preliminary analysis: when speculative batching merges a short-prefix and long-prefix request, the kernel remapper selects a different tiling order and applies rotary phase offsets assuming contiguous KV indexing. The speculative merge path did not re-normalize the phase offsets for requests that had different prefix lengths and chunk alignment, resulting in per-token positional phase shifts and hence different attention weighting. Floating-point divergence amplified by mixed-precision kernels (fp16 fused with fp32 reductions) in the remapped path.
proposed_fix: 1) On speculative merge, compute and store per-request rotary phase offsets before remapping and re-apply them after tile reordering. 2) Add a defensive verification pass in dev builds that checks phase invariants when kernel remap is used. 3) Add unit tests for merged-request rotary invariants and end-to-end quantized fp16 vs fp32 diff thresholds. 4) Consider disabling remap optimization for kernels with non-trivial rotary/rope semantics until invariant is proven safe.
tasks: T1: Create small repro harness that deterministically simulates merge ordering (Marcus)
T2: Patch remapper to carry rotary offsets as metadata and re-align after reorder (Marcus + Olivia)
T3: Add CI unit tests for merged-request rotary invariants (Riley)
T4: Add e2e numerical regression job that runs long-context traces nightly (Infra)
T5: Draft customer-facing incident note and mitigation steps (Asha)
T6: Performance validation that fix doesn't regress throughput beyond 3% (Perf Team)
notes: - This bug differs from prior KV-index corruption issues: no memory corruption observed; state remains consistent but computations are shifted.
- Repro is sensitive to accelerator scheduling; cannot rely solely on unit tests without simulating scheduling reorder.
- Mixed precision amplifies divergence; fp32-only runs reduce but do not eliminate the divergence, indicating algorithmic phase mismatch is primary.
- Short-term mitigation: set KERNEL_REMAP=0 or disable speculative batching for affected deployments.
- Long-term: formalize invariants for any kernel-level reordering that touches position-dependent ops (rotary/rope/relative-pos).
